Construction Contract

Contract submitted to owner:

___

___

Date: ___

Effective ___ TR Design Build, 134 Old Ridgefield Road, Wilton, CT hereinafter referred to as "Contractor", and ___, residing at: ___, hereinafter referred to as "Owner", enter into this construction contract whereby the Contractor shall perform the work described below hereinafter referred to as the "Work", and The Owner shall pay for the Work at the agreed upon price and at the agreed upon intervals set forth herein. The location of the Work, hereinafter referred to as the "Work Site" is: ___. The work will be performed and coordinated in accordance with the specifications, terms, and conditions outlined in this construction contract. The work will also be performed and coordinated in accordance with the specifications, terms, and conditions outlined in the "Approved Drawings," by TR Design Build dated ___. The work description that follows is intended to clarify any uncertain specifications and will supersede the drawings where there is a conflict. Any work or materials not explicitly stated or described in this contract is not included. All additional work will be put in writing and agreed upon by both parties before proceeding.

Scope of Work

Final Agreement and Scope of Work

During the design and pre-construction process, the Owner may communicate with multiple members in the design, estimating, and production teams. Preliminary discussions, design concepts, preferences, requests, sketches, emails, meeting notes, and verbal statements may change, be revised, or be replaced as the project develops.

The final Contract, approved drawings, and allowances collectively represent the Contractor's understanding of the work the Owner has authorized and the work included in the Contract Price. These documents supersede all prior discussions, representations, requests, concepts, and communications, whether oral or written.

Any work, material, feature, or selection not expressly included in the Contract Documents shall be considered excluded. If the Owner requests such work after execution of the Contract, it shall be addressed through a written Change Order and may result in an adjustment to the Contract Price and Project Schedule.

Permits

Permits expenses vary from town to town, and as a result, no value has been included in this contract for these costs. Permit expenses include all town and state departmental fees like, building, health, engineering, etc. Permit expenses also include any additional septic testing, drainage design or drainage certification required by the town. Upon receipt of an accepted contract and completion of the permit set of drawings, Contractor will promptly secure all permits necessary for the proposed scope of work. Contractor will pay the permit fees on behalf of the Owner and submit a request for payment to the Owner in the form of a Change Order.

Planning

Permits

Permits expenses vary from town to town, and as a result, no value has been included in this contract for these costs. Permit expenses include all town and state departmental fees like, building, health, engineering, etc. Upon receipt of an accepted contract and completion of the permit set of drawings, Contractor will promptly secure all permits necessary for the proposed scope of work. Contractor will pay the permit fees on behalf of the Owner and submit a request for payment to the Owner in the form of a Change Order.

Job Site Facilities

Portable Rest Room

A portable restroom will be provided by the Contractor at the Contractor's expense for the workers for the duration of the project.

Job Site Communication

Wireless Access

Contractor will need access to the residence password to access wi-fi at the job site in order to effectively communicate and conduct business with all those involved in the project.

Hazardous Materials

Lead Testing

Prior to the start of our work the proposed demolition area will be tested for lead.

In the event that lead is present, all demolition and removal of said contaminated materials will be handled in a manner consistent with the EPA RRP rules and practice.

The additional cost of lead removal is not included in this contract.

Asbestos

This contract does not include the cost to remove any asbestos. Any asbestos that requires removal/disruption to execute our scope of work will need to be abated by a licensed abatement contractor.

Protection

Protective Products

Provide dust walls as required

Furnish and install protective products over new and existing floor surfaces as required

Furnish and install 6 mil poly dust walls and zippers at all construction entrances to the work area

Air cleaner to be on-site during heavy dust times

Furnish and install duct filters at all returns within the workspace

Protect stairs and railings with foam roll as required

Project Preparation

Personal Property

Owner is responsible for clearing all personal property from the proposed work space(s) prior to commencement of the work.

Alarms

The Owner is responsible for having their alarm company bypass all security and smoke alarm equipment in rooms that are being gutted or areas that are impacting existing alarm equipment.

Sump Pumps

All existing sump pumps by code must be on GFCI outlets

The owner is responsible for having all sump pumps on labeled/dedicated circuits so they do not run the risk of being tripped accidentally during construction

TR can help coordinate re-wiring of sumps upon request

Demolition

Dumpsters & Dumping

Dumpsters will be provided by the Contractor at the Contractors expense for the removal and disposal of all debris associated with the project.

Concealed Existing Conditions

The Contract Price is based upon visible conditions and information reasonably available at the time this proposal was prepared. The Contract Price does not include the cost to relocate, modify, repair, or replace concealed or unforeseen existing conditions. If concealed conditions are encountered that require additional labor, materials, engineering, redesign, or coordination in order to complete the Work in a safe and code-compliant manner, such work shall constitute additional work and will be authorized and billed through a written Change Order.

Engineering

Structural Engineer

All engineering fees are excluded from the contract and will be billed separately to the Owner as a change order should they be required.

Supervision

This project will be supervised by a TR Design Build project manager. The responsibilities of supervision include:

— Opening and closing the job site each day

— Cleaning the job site at the close of each day

— Overseeing all trade partners performances

— Ordering materials (not including items supplied by homeowners)

— Scheduling of trades and material deliveries

— Maintaining the planned schedule

— Weekly job site meetings with home owner

— Overseeing that the job site is kept safe & organized to prevent injury

Exclusions

Items not included:

— Irrigation systems

— Smoke and CO detectors

— Security alarm systems

— Appliances

— Televisions / AV equipment

— Permit Fees / Town Fees / State Fees / Variances

— Existing code violations or inspector required repairs

— High end paints such as Farrow & Ball or similar

— Landscaping and landscape lighting

— Ledge removal, boulder removal, rock hammering, blasting

— Asbestos removal

— Lead removal

— Structural, Civil, and Survey Engineering Fees

— Movement in wood products due to inconsistent relative humidity levels

— Anything not clearly defined in the contract descriptions

Change Orders

TR Design-Build invests substantial time and resources during the Design and Pre-Construction phases to fully develop the construction drawings and contract documents before construction begins. Owner-requested changes during construction should be regarded as the exception rather than the normal course of the Project.

Any modification to the Contract Documents shall be processed as a written Change Order. Each Change Order shall identify: a detailed description of the requested change; any increase or decrease in the Contract Sum; the impact on the Project Schedule; and any additional costs associated with the requested modification. No Change Order shall become effective until it has been approved in writing by both the Owner and the Contractor. Approved Change Orders shall be invoiced in full during the next scheduled billing cycle.

Allowances Policy

Allowance values are place holders for items not finalized at the time of the contract. It is the Contractors responsibility to purchase all allowance items. Delivery expenses of Allowance items shall be included in the Allowance total. Allowance items that cost less than the value indicated in the contract will result in a credit to the Owner for the difference. Allowance items that cost more than the value indicated in the contract will result in a charge to the Owner for the difference. This allowance reconciliation will be part of the final invoice.

Insurance

Contractor shall at its own expense, procure and maintain public and general liability insurance. Contractor shall procure and maintain a builder's risk policy for the full insurable value of this project. The cost for the Builders Risk policy is included in your construction contract. The Owner shall bear the risk of all loss or damage from whatever cause including, by way of example, loss or damage caused by fire, theft or vandalism provided any such loss is not caused by the negligence of the Contractor.

Disputes

All claims or disputes between Contractor and Owner arising out of, or relating to the contract documents or breach thereof, shall be decided by arbitration in accordance with the Construction Arbitration Rules of the American Arbitration Association unless the parties mutually agree otherwise. All arbitration proceedings shall be held before one (1) arbitrator in Fairfield County, Connecticut and the law of the State of Connecticut shall be applicable to these proceedings.

Warranty

Contractor hereby warrantees their work against defects in workmanship and materials for a term of 1 year from the date of completion. Warranted materials would include framing lumber, siding and exterior trim materials, and interior trim materials. Products such as windows, roofing materials, electrical fixtures, plumbing fixtures, thermostats, transformers, motors, and heating elements would be covered under the manufacture's warrantees. This warranty shall not be deemed to include such imperfections as the result from normal settling, shrinkage, drying out, or acts of God or expiration of manufacturers' warrantees.

Material Escalation

If, during the performance of the contract, the price of the material significantly increases, through no fault of the contractor, the price shall be equitably adjusted by an amount reasonably necessary to cover any such significant price increases. As used herein, a significant price increase shall mean any increase in price exceeding 3% experienced by the contractor from the date of the contract signing.

Time Frame

Contractor estimates this project will take roughly ___ to complete barring any unforeseen circumstances due to delays from inclement weather, acts of God, or any other circumstances beyond our control.

Estimated start date is: ___

Estimated completion is: ___

Your dedicated field supervisor will provide you with a weekly schedule that will include a 3-week look ahead so you will always remain informed and up to date on the schedule and important milestones involving your project.

Acceptance of Drawings

By signing this contract the Owner acknowledges receipt of a digital or hard copy of the latest drawings referenced in this contract and authorizes the contractor to start ordering all necessary materials required to execute the drawings. Construction elements that the Owner requests be changed after being ordered or built will be charged as a change order to the Owner for the cost to remove and rebuild the said items.
